_comment:
Focused cgroup bandwidth-throttling demonstration. A single cgroup '/throttled' is given a strict 10% quota (cpu.max '10000 100000' = 10ms quota per 100ms period). Two CPU-greedy tasks live inside it and would consume ~2 full CPUs without throttling — but the cgroup_bw enforcement path will repeatedly throttle and unthrottle them so their aggregate CPU consumption stays under 10ms per 100ms wall window. A third task 'free' lives in the root cgroup and is unconstrained; it should make smooth forward progress regardless of what the throttled cgroup is doing. Compare cgroup_hierarchy.json (which contrasts /background vs /interactive at 20% quota with mixed task profiles) — this example is narrower: one throttled cgroup, one free task, clear before/after the throttle fires.

Run with -s lavd to exercise the LAVD cgroup-bw path (the simple scheduler has no cgroup awareness). Add --verbose-summary to see per-cgroup throttle counters.
_run_units: rt-app 'run'/'sleep' are microseconds; cpu.max is '<quota_us> <period_us>' (cgroup-v2 convention).
